title: Mountain Villa Bandaged Man Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Sonoko) omitted by convention, matching the v1 scaffold's own grouping. This creates two gaps that can't be represented as edges: the accidental door-opening where Ran glimpses Takahashi's real (slim) build, and his two follow-up attacks on her to keep her silent -- both captured instead as attrs/detail text on Takahashi's node and on the room edges, since the other party (Ran) has no node. No `event` node type. Honest gap: no red-herring motive material exists in the transcript for Ota, Sumiya, or Ayako -- none of them are shown with any grievance against Chikako, so has_motive_against is left on the culprit only for this case; the red herring here is structural (everyone was 'inside the lodge' when the bandaged man appeared outside, seemingly clearing all of them) rather than a false motive. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: It was pouring rain when the bandaged man supposedly climbed a tree onto the balcony and broke into Ran's room, yet there are no muddy tracks anywhere inside -- inconsistent with someone actually climbing in from outside in a storm.

On the second break-in, the window is smashed but one of its locks is already undone -- if an intruder had really broken the glass to get in, the lock should still be latched. It was unlocked from the inside first, then the glass was broken afterward to fake outside entry.

Two distinct wire-groove marks are cut into the central balcony's outside railing -- consistent with a two-wire rig used to swing an object past a window and retrieve it, not with any person's actual passage.

Chikako's choker turns up by the front door after the bandaged man supposedly carried her straight into the forest -- proving her body (or at least her head) passed back through the lodge itself, which only someone already inside could have arranged.

Ran describes tackling a bandaged man with an average, unremarkable build, but Takahashi is known by the whole group as noticeably overweight -- a mismatch that only makes sense if his usual bulk is fake padding, hollow at the moment of the attack because his abdomen was occupied by Chikako's head instead.

Chikako's slippers are found at the back door, not the front, even though she was seen retreating to her room -- she must have deliberately snuck out the back, unseen, matching the theory that a note lured her outside quietly rather than her leaving normally.
